READABILITY.evidence: Names reveal intent (encryptWriter, decryptReader, writeHeader, flush, finish, decodeKey, deriveKey). The package doc lays out the stream format, and exported funcs have doc comments. The only small blemish is the abbreviated name `recordBf`.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: Functions are short and Validate is cleanly table-driven. But config.go imports stdlib "crypto/pbkdf2" instead of the vendored golang.org/x/crypto/pbkdf2 the conventions call for. And storage.PathGenerator hardcodes encrypt=false, so the handler needs its own separate path generator.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Chunk length is bounds-checked (`length < nonceSize+tagSize || length > maxRecord`) and the HMAC uses constant-time hmac.Equal. Truncation maps to ErrUnexpectedEOF, the key is copied, Close is idempotent with sticky errors, and constants are named. Errors are wrapped with %w around ErrInvalidKey.

C7-13-CASE1.evidence: fileutil signatures changed as mandated, and unencrypted output and YAML keys are unchanged. But storage.PathGenerator keeps its old signature and always passes false for encryption, so the handler routes .enc naming through its own generator. It works, but it is an awkward way to update the caller.
